comparison: Auto and forced Spectral return the same full complex state vector for exp(-itL) from one prepared complex initial state.
order: Both variants execute in each fresh process; order reverses with parity of process_index + case_index + batch_index. Setup, preparation, and query phases share this order convention.
setup: Graph construction and initial-state generation are separately recorded once. Plan setup includes validation, dispatch, dense construction and any full eigendecomposition; it excludes graph generation. Five warmed plan constructors are timed for each variant. The last plans are used for subsequent work.
preparation: Five prepare_state calls are timed per variant; each computes the spectral overlaps or complete-graph mean. Fresh final prepared states are then reused for all timed queries.
queries: Fixed repetitions cycle through all 16 predeclared times. Every distinct vector output is validated componentwise before any query timings. Timed loops black_box the complete returned vector and accumulate one varying component into a checksum. Allocation, return-value validation, black_box, checksum addition and vector destruction are included; setup, state preparation, correctness validation, warmup, JSON serialization and process startup are excluded.
input_state: re_i=((17*i+3)%29)-14; im_i=((11*i+5)%23)-11; normalize by sqrt(sum_i(re_i^2+im_i^2)); no RNG.
graph: Both directed entries of each positive edge; no diagonal or duplicate entries. Degrees accumulate neighbours in ascending index order. Clique weights are constant. Near-clique uses twice the declared weight on edge {0,1}. Path has nearest-neighbour edges only.
summary: For each case and fresh process, take median(Spectral_ns / Auto_ns) across paired query batches. Across processes report the median and observed minimum/maximum. Also retain setup and preparation pairs. No confidence interval, statistical significance, cross-machine prediction or whole-engine improvement is claimed.
